name: vscode-tcp-client
description: Send and receive TCP messages from VS Code with escape-sequence support

tcpClient.connection.timeoutMs.markdownDescription: Connect attempt timeout in milliseconds. Set to 0 to disable.

tcpClient.variables.custom.markdownDescription: User-defined variables that can be inserted into outgoing messages via `{{name}}` syntax. Each entry has a `name` (the reference) and a `value` (the literal substitution). Built-in variables like `{{timestamp}}` are always available and cannot be overridden.

tcpClient.variables.timestampFormat.markdownDescription: Format pattern for the built-in `{{timestamp}}` variable. Supports `YYYY` (year), `MM` (month), `DD` (day), `HH` (hour), `mm` (minute), `ss` (second), `sss` (millisecond), and `Z` (UTC marker). Other characters are treated as literals. Default: ISO 8601 with milliseconds.

id.description: Unique identifier for this envelope. Used internally as the lookup key. Must be unique across all custom envelopes and must not collide with the built-in envelope ids (`none`, `hl7-mllp`, `hl7-llp`).

label.description: Human-readable name shown in the envelope dropdown.

prefix.description: Bytes prepended to the payload (escape-sequence string: `\xHH`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\\`, `\0`). Empty by default.

suffix.description: Bytes appended to the payload (escape-sequence string). Empty by default.

linePrefix.description: Bytes prepended to every `\n`-separated line of the payload (escape-sequence string). When both `linePrefix` and `lineSuffix` are empty, the payload is wrapped once with the outer prefix/suffix — the default.

lineSuffix.description: Bytes appended to every `\n`-separated line of the payload (escape-sequence string). Use this for per-line terminators like `\r` (HL7) or `\n`.

tcpClient.envelopes.custom.markdownDescription: User-defined envelopes. Each entry defines a framing preset (prefix + suffix + optional per-line prefix/suffix) that appears alongside the built-ins in the panel dropdown. Built-ins are not removable from here — they live in code. Use the **TCP Client** section of the Settings UI to add, edit, or remove entries; changes are saved to `settings.json` automatically.

scripts.pretest: npm run compile && npm run lint:webview
